newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico plans to boost oil production budget.
newsitem.headline: Mexico plans to boost oil production budget.

text.p: State-owned oil giant Petroleos Mexicanos plans to increase 1997 exploration and production investment 64.9 percent from year-ago levels, the government said.
The planned 1996 E&P investment budget was $2.3 billion, suggesting that E&P investment in 1997 would rise to $3.79 billion.
The government did not specify what 1996 E&P investment figure the increase would be based on, and Pemex officials were unable to give details.
Since the 1996 figure was itself an increase in planned investment of 57.3 percent over the previous year, though, the government is clearly making a giant push to pump more oil.

"The numbers seem high, but the potential for export is there, so with the present price structure it makes sense to produce more oil," said John Lichtblau, chairman of the Petroleum Industry Research Foundation.

Analysts hailed the 1997 budgeted increase in exploration and production investment, saying it follows a Pemex spending lag in the early 1990s. In recent years the Mexican government has been compensating for the lapse in exploration, they said.

"The numbers are encouraging," said Rafael Quijano, director for Latin America and Brazil at Petroleum Finance Corp. "I hope they can sustain this kind of investment because there is plenty of oil to be developed in Mexico."
Quijano said Pemex could profitably boost exploration spending further for the next ten years.
The oil company expects crude oil production in 1997 to increase to an average 3.08 million barrels daily, compared with 2.86 million barrels daily average in 1996.
Higher oil prices and the expectation that prices will remain elevated through 1997 could be motivating boosted investment, industry observers said.
In refining activity, a 42.7 percent real increase is planned for 1997, the government said. Programmed investment for 1996 was $933 million, up 5.8 percent from 1995.
Quijano said next year's increased refining focus reflects spending on the $1 billion project to upgrade the Cadereyta refinery near Monterrey, Nuevo Leon.
Pemex should spend an extra 33.9 percent in gas and basic petrochemicals in 1997, the government said. Programmed investment was $182 million in 1996.
Gas and basic petrochemical investment rose 74 percent in 1996 from the previous year.
Funds will be needed in the company's natural gas division to finance plans to replace the Cactus complex destroyed in an explosion earlier this year.
On Wednesday the oil company plans to give a press conference to further outline 1997 spending plans, a Pemex spokeswoman said.
